Darshna Devi and another  ...Appellan  Vs.
 Jagan Nath and others

...Respondent(
 CORAM: HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE NIDHI GUPTA  Present:- Mr. Vijay Lath, Advocate and  Mr. Naveen Sharma (Moudgil), Advocate  for the appellants.

Mr. D.P.Gupta, Advocate and  Mr. Shubham Gupta, Advocate  for respondent No.3.
 ***
 NIDHI GUPTA, J.
The present appeal has been filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.8,26,000/- awarded by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rupnagar (hereinafter referred to as "the learned Tribunal") vide Award dated 14.09.2018 passed in MACT Case No. 305 dated 31.05.2016 filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, (hereinafter referred to as "the Act").
The two claimants are 42-year-old mother and 48-year-old father of the deceased Vijay Kumar, who was 22 years old at the time of accident.

2. Brief facts of the case are that the learned Tribunal on the basis of pleadings and evidence adduced before it concluded that the deceased-Vijay Kumar had died due to the injuries suffered by him in a motor vehicular accident that took place on 28.04.2016 at about 10:30 a.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of a Tipper bearing registration No.PB-65-Z-6939 (hereinafter "the offending vehicle") being driven by respondent No.1; owned by respondent No.2; and insured by respondent No.3.
The learned Tribunal awarded the above said compensation along with interest @ 7% per annum.
All the respondents were held liable to pay the said compensation jointly and severally.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants seeks enhancement of compensation by submitting that the income of the deceased has been taken on the lower side as only Rs.7,000/-p.m. as that of an unskilled labourer.
It is submitted that deceased was working as a Poclane Operator.

Thus, as per Darshna Devi And Anr vs Jagan Nath And Ors on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164212923/
1 the relevant Notification dated 11.10.2017 issued by office of Labour Commissioner, Punjab,
minimum wage of the deceased ought to have been taken as Rs.8,887.52 p.m., as that of skilled worker.

entities.text: Darshna Devi And Anr vs Jagan Nath And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, as per the said Notification, minimum wage of even unskilled labourer is Rs.7,210.52 p.m.
Thus, income of the deceased deserves to be enhanced.
A copy of the said Notification is handed over in Court today, which is taken on record.
He further submits that even nothing has been awarded by way of future prospects; and parental consortium has also not been granted to appellant No.2.
It is accordingly prayed that present Appeal be allowed; and the awarded compensation be enhanced in the above terms.

4. Per contra, ld. counsel for respondent No.3 opposes submissions made on behalf of the appellants and submits that impugned Award suffers from no infirmity as the compensation awarded to the appellants is just and fair.
Hence, present Appeal deserves to be dismissed.
5. No other argument is raised on behalf of the parties.
I have heard ld. counsel and perused the case file in detail.

6. Perusal of the record of the case shows that it was the pleaded case of the appellants before the learned Tribunal that the deceased was working as Poclane Operator and was earning Rs.25,000/-
p.m.
However, it was admitted by claimant No.1/mother of the deceased/PW1 in her cross-examination that she had no documents to prove income of her deceased son as Poclane Operator.

Accordingly, learned Tribunal had taken income of the deceased as Rs.7,000/-p.m. on the basis of relevant notification, as per which minimum wages for labourers revised w.e.f. 01.03.2015 are Rs.6,847.65 rounded off to Rs.7,000/- p.m.

Reliance of the appellants on the Notification dated 11.10.2017 is misplaced as, as per the said Notification, the said rate of minimum wages is applicable w.e.f. 01.09.2017; whereas in the present case, date of accident is 28.04.2016.
As such, I find no error in the income as assessed by the learned Tribunal.
7. Further, age of the deceased was determined to be 22 years on the date of accident on the basis of his Postmortem Report Ex.P5.

Accordingly, learned Tribunal had correctly made a deduction of 50%
towards personal expenses; thereby calculating annual income to be Rs.42,000/- p.a. (Rs.3,500 x 12).
Learned Tribunal had further correctly applied multiplier of 18 and calculated total dependency to be Rs.7,56,000 (Rs.42,000 x 18).

The Tribunal has further awarded Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses; Rs.40,000/- towards consortium to claimant No.1; and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate; thereby granting total compensation of Rs.8,26,000.
However, learned Tribunal has awarded nothing towards future prospects as per the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in "Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation" Law Finder Doc ID # 188882.

8. In view of the above discussion, present appeal is partly allowed; and compensation awarded to the appellants is modified in the following manner: -
